content:
Having trouble using Signal on multiple devices at the same time? This encrypted messaging service is making it easier for users to use the app across different iPhones and more devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to their existing Signal account, rather than being limited to setting up secondary mobile devices as iPads.

The company also announced Android linking support today, stating: "We are expanding linked device support on iOS so that you can link an iPhone to your Signal account, and our support for iPad will continue."

When linking an additional iPhone, users can choose whether to transfer the complete message history, as well as media content stored within the past 45 days.

Signal stated that the entire transfer process uses full end-to-end encryption, and employs the same "link-and-sync" technology used for iPads and desktop devices (including the Signal app for Mac).

For users who need to use separate work and personal iPhones, or who test multiple devices simultaneously, this expanded support is particularly useful.

This update also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to Apple's Messages ecosystem, where conversations sync seamlessly across iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Signal for iOS version 8.22 is currently rolling out on the App Store. Signal previously introduced a username feature, allowing users to contact each other without sharing phone numbers.
